── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 24, 27, 37, 53 mi
This week: 40 mi over 5 runs.
Body: "Legs a bit heavy early in the week, fine by Thursday."
Asks: "My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: This week focuses on a steady build with a marathon-pace quality run and a longer easy run, keeping volume moderate to manage fatigue.
Answers: I’d not recommend jumping to 80 miles a week. That’s a lot of volume and can lead to over-training, especially if you’re doing it twice a day.
Next week:
Mon: rest
Tue: easy, 5.5 mi, heart rate under 150, flat route. Keeps legs fresh after rest.
Wed: quality, 9 mi with 6 at marathon pace, keep effort at target pace.
Thu: easy, 5.5 mi, heart rate under 150, moderate hill terrain. Restes the legs.
Fri: rest
Sat: easy, 5.5 mi, heart rate under 150, low-intensity. Provides steady mileage.
Sun: long, 18 mi, easy pace, heart rate under 150. Builds endurance without hard work.
